title: Inference Performance Lab
summary: A benchmark harness that compares hosted and local inference, CPU and GPU, quantization levels, caching, batching, and speculative decoding on quality, latency, throughput, memory, and cost, then recommends a configuration for a stated workload.
primaryMessage: I understand the operational economics of model serving and choose systems by workload constraints, not model popularity.

executive.problem: Teams pick a model and serving setup by reputation, then discover it is too slow, too expensive, or needs hardware they do not have.
executive.approach: Run the same workloads across hosted and local options and serving techniques, measure quality alongside speed and cost, and select the cheapest configuration that meets the workload's targets.
executive.impact: Serving decisions come with numbers: latency percentiles, throughput, memory, cost per thousand requests, and quality on the task.
executive.whyItMatters: Shows the operational side of AI engineering that determines whether a feature is affordable and fast enough to ship.

problem: Model serving choices trade quality against latency, throughput, memory, and cost. Quantization saves memory but can hurt quality; batching raises throughput but can raise tail latency; long contexts change everything. Without a controlled harness, teams cannot compare options on their own workload.
users: Product teams choosing a serving setup

constraints.detail: Same prompts, same scoring, fixed seeds where possible, and recorded hardware for every run.
Cost modelled from hosted pricing or hardware amortization, with assumptions shown.
A configuration that fails the task-quality floor is rejected regardless of speed.

architectureNotes: Every run records model version, runner version, hardware, quantization, and settings, so results are comparable and repeatable.
The selector filters out configurations below the quality floor or above the latency target, then ranks the rest by cost.

aiTechnique.choice: Controlled benchmarking of serving methods: quantization, batching, caching, and speculative decoding across hosted and local runtimes.
aiTechnique.rationale: Serving methods interact with workload shape, so the only reliable way to choose is to measure on representative workloads with quality scored in the same run.

rejected.reason: Measure quality on generic tasks and ignore latency, hardware, and cost for your workload.
Usually measured on favorable settings that do not match production traffic.

implementation.detail: Workload definitions in YAML; a load generator for concurrency and batch sweeps.
Adapters for hosted APIs, vLLM on GPU, and llama.cpp on CPU behind one interface.
Time to first token, inter-token latency, p50/p95/p99, tokens per second, peak memory, and cost per 1K requests.
Task-specific scorers run on the same outputs that were timed.
Prometheus exporters and Grafana dashboards for GPU and runtime metrics.
Pareto charts of quality against latency and cost, and a recommended configuration per workload.

datasets: Synthetic long-context documents for context-length scaling

metrics.name: p95 latency
metrics.method: Load generator with fixed request mix

metrics.name: Throughput (tokens/s)
metrics.method: Output tokens over wall time at steady state

metrics.name: Cost per 1K requests
metrics.method: Pricing or amortized hardware cost with stated assumptions

metrics.name: Supported context length
metrics.target: e.g. 32K tokens within memory and latency limits

regression: Benchmark reruns on runtime or model upgrades
Alerts when p95 latency or quality moves outside tolerance
failureAnalysis: Out-of-memory and timeout failures logged per configuration
Quality drops traced to specific task types

humanControl.detail: Cost and hardware assumptions are shown next to every cost figure.
The selector recommends; an engineer signs off on the production configuration.

expected: A quantized local configuration meets the quality floor at lower cost for some workloads
Batching and caching improve throughput with a measurable tail-latency cost

limitations: Results apply to the hardware, versions, and workloads tested.
Cost models depend on pricing and utilization assumptions.
Does not cover multi-node serving or autoscaling behavior.
32K context support is pending a runtime experiment.

setup: docker compose exec bench python -m lab.run --workload workloads/qa.yaml --runners vllm,llamacpp
docker compose exec bench python -m lab.report
reproduction.testData: Workload YAML files and prompt sets under workloads/.
reproduction.credentials: Optional hosted API keys in .env; local runners need none.
reproduction.expectedOutput: A results table, Pareto charts, and a recommended configuration per workload.

capabilities.name: Quality, latency, throughput, memory, and cost
